result:
Copying isn't the right move here — it creates two homes for one idea, and currency formatting is exactly the kind of logic where silent divergence (one team tweaks rounding, the other doesn't) turns into real financial-display bugs between invoices and reports. The cross-module coupling you're trying to avoid isn't actually solved by copying either; it's solved by giving the shared logic a third, neutral home that neither team owns.

Put it in a top-level `shared/` (or `common/`) folder — e.g. `shared/formatting/formatCurrency.js` — as one of the small set of approved shared roots in your tree. Both `reports/` and `billing/` import from `shared/`, so neither depends on the other, but there's still a single source of truth. If the teams later need genuinely different formatting rules, that's a sign to fork it into two differently-named functions (e.g. `formatCurrencyForInvoice` vs `formatCurrencyForPdf`), not to silently duplicate the same name in two places.
